                         WHITIS LAND INVESTMENTS, LP’S REPLY BRIEF

           Whitis Land Investments, LP (“Whitis”) submits this Reply Brief pursuant to SOAH Order
No. 6 and would show the following:

           I.       INTRODUCTION

           Whitis submits this Reply Brief in response to arguments raised in the Initial Brief of
Christopher Landgraf. Whitis contends that those arguments: (a) place a less than proportionate
weight on community values, (b) highlight flaws in the Joint Applicants’ cost estimates, and (c)
make assumptions regarding subdivision development that are not supported by the record. As
such, the ALJs and the Commission should weigh all routes in this proceeding under PURA and
the Commission’s substantive rules and select Route Whitis 1-14 in this docket or a route that does
not utilize Link F1.

           II.      REPLY TO CHRISTOPHER LANDGRAF

           1.       Mr. Landgraf argues that individual properties under active development but not
having broken ground should be given less weight.1 Limiting the consideration of development to
a binary test of whether the development has broken ground or not unnecessarily limits the impact

1
    Initial Post-Hearing Brief of Christopher Landgraf at 5-6.


Intervenor: Whitis Land Investments, LP
Reply Brief                                                                              Page 1 of 6
 that single-family subdivisions have on a particular community. Instead, developments that have
not broken ground are more appropriately viewed through the lenses of community values and
cost.

                  Community Values

         2.       The need for affordable single-family homes, as well as present and future land use,
are community values that must be considered by both the ALJs and the Commission.2 Whitis’s
property is a large tract under development comprised of approximately 3,800 lots.3 The record
shows that the Joint Applicants established their own preference for some future subdivisions
based on the community value of future land use; Whitis is asking for no more consideration than
what has already been given to others in this case.4

                  Cost

         3.       Entitlements, such Municipal Utility Districts, which Mr. Landgraf specifically
mentions,5 significantly increase the constructability and value of the property. By Joint Applicants
performing cost estimates that do not consider existing entitlements, the cost estimates fall short
and become unreliable. Whitis and Solana Ranch are situated next to each other along Link F1.6
Both parties have secured multiple entitlements.7 Routes 894 and 487, and any route utilizing Link
F1, fails to account for any cost beyond the base land costs for removing a 200-foot-wide swath
of entitled, developable land from two adjacent communities comprised of approximately 18,000
single family lots, collectively.8 Therefore, the cost estimate for any route utilizing Link F1 do not
estimate its true cost. The ALJs and the Commission should consider those underestimates in their
consideration of all routes utilizing Link F1.

                  Subdivision Development

  Transcript Vol. 2 at 27:16-22.
3
  WL Ex. 1 at Exh. BW-4 at 1.

Reply Brief                                                                                 Page 2 of 6
         4.        Mr. Landgraf also questions the value of homes built near the 765kV line, as well
as the compatibility of affordable single-family lots with an airstrip.9 Both arguments rely on
assumptions. The assumptions are not based on actual costs of homes near 765kV transmission
lines or whether affordable single-family lots can coexist with an airstrip. They are simply
conjecture and should be treated as such by the ALJs and the Commission. Nevertheless, Whitis
addresses each below because the record reflects a different reality than Mr. Landgraf’s questions
suggest.

                 Home Values

        5.       Constructing transmission lines along Link F1 will reduce the amount of
developable land in the Salado area, thereby adversely impacting the availability of affordable
single-family development. Mr. Landgraf assumes that if the transmission line were built along
Link F1 new homes built near the line would be less expensive than if the transmission line were
built elsewhere.10 Unfortunately, that ignores the financial realities of subdivision development.
The record supports that lot projections informed Whitis’s decisions to pursue a MUD and
discharge permit with the TCEQ.11 If the transmission line were built utilizing Links E52 and F1,
at least 672 single family residential lots would be impacted.12 With fewer developable acres
available in the area, the cost of single-family residential homes will rise as a simple function of
supply and demand.

                 Compatibility

        6.       Mr. Landgraf also questions the compatibility of an airstrip with affordable single-
family homes. The size of Whitis’s land provides enough space to accommodate affordable single-
family lots, custom home lots, and an airstrip to serve the subdivision. Whitis’s subdivision
included in WLI Ex. 1 at Exh. BW-4 is approximately 1.8 miles at its greatest length from north
to south and approximately 1.3 miles at its greatest width. This subdivision is equivalent to the

12

Reply Brief                                                                                Page 3 of 6
 size of all downtown Austin, combined with the University of Texas campus, which is large enough
space to include a broad variety of land uses.

        7.       Furthermore, Whitis has constructed subdivisions with this exact variety on more
than one occasion.13 Three Creeks, a Bell County subdivision designed and built by Whitis and
located approximately 12 miles north of Link F1, contains numerous lots designed as affordable
single-family lots alongside numerous lots exceeding 1 acre in size, which were designed for
custom single-family homes.14 The Three Creeks layout is embedded in this document below, and
for demonstrative purposes, larger custom lots are highlighted in yellow and affordable single
family lots are shown in white.15




        8.       The majority of lots depicted in the Three Creeks exhibit are of a similar width as
the majority of the lots that Whitis is using in its subdivision in this case.16 The presence of larger,


13
   See WLI Ex. 1 at Exh. BW-8 (Three Creeks Layout 4).
14
   Id.
15
   Id.

Intervenor: Whitis Land Investments, LP
Reply Brief                                                                                  Page 4 of 6
 acre lots suitable for premium, custom homes in a small section of the overall project did not
influence, limit, or prevent the construction of affordable housing in the majority of Three Creeks.
In addition, it is not uncommon for an airstrip to exist near custom homes. Here, Whitis’s
development sequence places the airstrip before construction of any residential lots. Whitis, a
developer with decades of experience, provided evidence of completed projects with a variety of
lot sizes. The ALJs and the Commission should apply the weight that the evidence warrants when
deciding this case.

        III.     CONCLUSION

        9.       Speculative arguments should not be given weight by the ALJs or the Commission.
Moreover, entitlements to land along Link F1 have fundamentally changed the constructability and
value of Whitis land and necessitate consideration in selection of the final route in this case.
Because Joint Applicants failed to include such changes in cost estimates for routes utilizing Link
F1, those estimates drastically underestimate ROW acquisition cost and are unreliable, as a result.
Fortunately, the ALJs and the Commission have an alternative that avoids these issues. Route
Whitis 1-14:
                 a.   is approximately $35.7 million less and 7.26 miles shorter than Route 894;
                 b. has 105.7 miles not parallel to compatible ROW, while Route 894 has 125.15
                      miles; and
                 c. avoids multiple developments in the Salado area.

Therefore, Whitis requests that the ALJs and the Commission select Route Whitis 1-14 in this
docket, and if not, then avoid any route utilizing Link F1.
